## What's new

Threadnote 5.0.0 turns working context into a verifiable lifecycle across agents, from reviewed closeout to health checks, CI, procedures, and private value reports.

### Resumable one-command setup

`threadnote setup <surface>` now previews one deterministic local setup plan; `--apply` initializes the core, current
repository manifest and seed, selected catalog integration and declared hooks, current code graph, doctor checks, and a
final source-backed Context Brief. A strict private `SetupReceiptV1` records only hashes, bounded operation state, and
recovery references, so interrupted plans resume safely and an unchanged completed apply is a no-op. `--undo` previews
receipt-owned rollback and `--undo --apply` removes only unchanged setup-created artifacts. Organization, composer, and
team-sharing setup remain outside this local workflow. Private value reports count applied setup starts, failures,
completions, supported-agent reuse, and bounded time to the verified Context Brief without recording tasks or paths.

### Guided two-agent activation

`threadnote activate start|continue|status|undo` introduces a preview-first, resumable activation receipt for two
distinct catalog surfaces in one local/offline journey. It previews bounded AGENTS/guidance and ADR imports, configures
both surfaces, creates the local Git team share, compiles a source-verified Context Brief, and stops at separate import,
Knowledge Delta application, and direct-publication or Git-proposal approvals. Its deterministic plan binds observed
catalog, repository, source-set, task, and team-share identities as hashes only; private state contains no task text,
source or repository paths, remote URLs, credentials, or customer data. Continuation re-observes those inputs, records
each operation with revision CAS, and safely resumes interrupted direct publication or local proposal materialization.
Undo remains preview-first and may reverse only unchanged activation-created receipts.

Cross-agent proof never synthesizes a successful retrieval or accepts pasted observation JSON. Activation names the
secondary catalog surface and emits one opaque challenge for its installed local MCP runtime; the runtime reads the
exact published decision only after bounded project-scoped recall discovers its URI and stable memory identity, then
writes a content-free, transport-attested receipt. Activation pauses until that receipt exists and rejects forged,
replayed, stale, wrong-surface, wrong-runtime, expired, or changed evidence. Local proposal
materialization never pushes without an explicit request, and organization-hosted deployment remains outside this
workflow. Structured decisions preserve rationale, constraints, performed verification, invalidated knowledge, and
unresolved risks through review, while idempotent local value events count activation, first evidence, completion, and
verified second-agent reuse without storing tasks, paths, or memory bodies.

### Project guidance import and projection

`threadnote guidance import <surface> --project <name>` previews existing adapter-declared project guidance and, with
`--apply`, creates or reuses a private Knowledge Delta candidate for review; it never approves or publishes. Approved
active durable memories can be explicitly projected with `threadnote guidance project ... --memory <uri>`, using
deterministic ordering plus a provenance- and hash-managed block. Status reports current, missing, modified, stale,
and evidence-unavailable targets, while preview-first removal preserves unmanaged content. Project-guidance support
now extends beyond the initial four surfaces and is declared by the canonical agent catalog, which reports each managed
target or an explicit unsupported reason. Shared physical targets use one target-owned receipt. Projection drift feeds
context health and Context Check. A second agent surface can reuse the same approved knowledge without separate
canonical copies.

### Reviewable health repairs and Git proposals

`threadnote context repair preview` now turns the bounded health report into deterministic, content-hash-bound repair
proposals without changing memory. `context repair apply` requires the exact proposal ID and revision plus `--approved`,
rechecks project and record preconditions, and uses a private recovery journal for safe retries. Automatic mutations are
limited to personal lifecycle-safe archives and exact removal of relations to direct personal URIs proven missing or
inactive; shared targets, stable identity aliases, ambiguous findings, citation repairs, guidance, preferences, and
smoke findings stay review-only. Equivalent preview/apply MCP tools preserve the same read-only versus destructive
boundary.

Semantic contradictions remain direction-neutral because analyzer ordering does not establish which record is stale.
After an explicit stale/current designation bound to the analyzer contradiction ID and exact report revision, preview
can include a review-only supersede suggestion only for exact canonical personal durable records with valid stable
identities. Its Knowledge Delta approval tuple binds that designation, the selected proposal IDs, revisions, and record
preconditions, and a separate reviewed lifecycle operation must preserve the stale identity under `status: superseded`
with `archived_from` provenance; health repair never performs this semantic change automatically.

Applied durable Knowledge Delta candidates can be exported with `threadnote share propose` or the read-only
`share_propose` MCP tool. The canonical provider-neutral artifact binds the review revision, exact Git base, approved
source hashes, configured team, portable remote repository identity, and absent-or-exact target CAS while preserving
portable relations and stable shared identity. Export does not create a branch, commit, pull request, provider object,
or network request; `--output` is an explicit local-only write.

Provider-neutral local materialization remains preview-first. Its explicit apply path rechecks the repository, base,
proposal, and target CAS bindings before creating the deterministic branch and commit, reuses an idempotent retry, and
never pushes, opens a pull request, or calls a hosted provider.

### Agent integration catalog

`threadnote agents list --json` now reports a catalog of 27 agent surfaces with setup guidance, capability boundaries,
platform coverage, and verification metadata. Managed integrations can be previewed, installed, repaired, inspected, and
removed through one lifecycle. New managed user-scope paths include Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Amp, and Factory Droid;
catalog-only and partial entries stay clearly marked instead of being presented as fully managed.

Personal Cursor Cloud bootstrap now installs only memory-oriented capabilities and guidance: it omits local graph MCP
tools, graph bootstrap instructions, and the graph skill because Cloud Agent checkouts are ephemeral. Organization
shared setup continues to use its separate local graph adapter, where shared graph work remains available.

### Fair multi-worktree graph scheduling

Concurrent code-graph builds now share a home-wide two-builder budget with checkout-aware scheduling, so one checkout is
less likely to occupy every build slot while another waits. Interactive requests retain priority, background work ages
into the same priority tier after a bounded wait, and live pre-5.0 builders continue to count safely during upgrades.

Build status, JSON output, and MCP progress now expose bounded queue position, admission class, active resource, blocker,
and cumulative phase and wait durations. This makes graph-readiness delays attributable without exposing repository
paths or source content. Materialization timing keeps scheduler admission wait separate from active attribution work,
so performance regressions remain actionable.

Ordinary MCP query, node, neighbors, and explain calls can continue immediately from an immutable compatible stale ready
snapshot while a durable refresh is active, queued, or deferred. Privacy-safe continuity reports opaque `cgdq_` tokens
and bounded retry guidance; path, impact, whole-graph analysis, and exact-current citations remain strict. Agents can
continue bounded discovery and verify exact source literals without tight polling. Durable latest-wins reduction,
irrevocable publication, and crash recovery converge to the newest demand.

### Reliable deferred code references

Deferred code citations now finalize up to four independent memories at a time while retaining deterministic receipts
and the existing per-memory safety fences. The CLI and MCP finalize commands perform one follow-up derived-index repair
for citations that actually finalized, reporting whether recall is current, intentionally unavailable, or deferred with
clear repair guidance. Doctor gives a bounded, privacy-safe pending-worktree attribution without revealing paths,
memory URIs, repository identities, or source locators.

### Lifecycle and closeout foundations

Task-only Context Briefs now keep the highest-ranked handoffs and durable decisions ahead of unrelated citation
metadata when fitting the response budget. Broad coordination and planning requests therefore retain useful project
context instead of spending the available space only on graph contracts and diagnostics, while explicit code-linked
briefs preserve their stronger source-first evidence priority.

Memory schema v5 adds optional ownership and `review_after` maintenance metadata. Bounded Knowledge Deltas and
`threadnote closeout preview/apply` make proposed context changes reviewable before they become durable knowledge.
Session closeout reviews may also carry an optional versioned structured contract with rationale, constraints,
verification performed, knowledge invalidated, and unresolved risks. The contract is backward-readable for older
reviews and is rendered into the reviewed durable candidate body, so edits and explicit approval continue to apply
exactly the text that was reviewed.

`threadnote context metadata preview|apply` and matching MCP tools now support maintenance-only updates to an active
personal durable memory. Preview binds the canonical URI or stable memory ID, current content hash, identity, and a
deterministic proposal/revision; apply requires explicit approval and rechecks all bindings under a memory lock. Each
of opaque `owner`, canonical ISO `review_after`, and explicit `valid_to` can be set, preserved, or independently
cleared without rewriting the memory body, citations, relations, or unrelated metadata. Shared, inactive, ambiguous,
malformed, and stale targets fail closed; this path never archives or retires knowledge.

`threadnote context health` reports stale citations, review dates, broken relations, duplicates, and pending conflicts in
text or JSON without mutating memory. `threadnote context check` provides deterministic text, JSON, and SARIF for direct
citations, exact-current reverse graph impact, active conflicts, cited-document gaps, and at most eight content-free
capture advisories. It never prepares a graph or reports clean when required graph evidence is incomplete.

Large text health reports now lead with total, shown, and omitted finding counts, group the bounded visible findings by
severity and category, show representative owning memories, and point to the next repair, graph-evidence, or structured
inspection step. Project-scale health reviews stay actionable without burying ownership and remaining work behind long
lists of citation IDs.

Context health now also performs bounded, deterministic semantic contradiction analysis across active durable memories.
It returns only content-free claim identities and fingerprints, keeps every semantic repair review-only, preserves
project and lifecycle isolation, and reports incomplete or filtered evidence as unknown instead of clean.

`threadnote context health aggregate` now combines personal-only project health with explicitly selected configured
Git team snapshots, or every configured team when no selector is supplied. It never fetches, syncs, or writes; team
files are read through bounded symlink-safe snapshot fences and matched to one clean Git revision. Missing, dirty,
raced, malformed, oversized, citation-unverifiable, or otherwise incomplete evidence reports unknown with exit 2
instead of clean. `context health schedule` and matching read-only MCP tools expose the same provider-neutral,
network-disabled invocation and exit-code contract for local schedulers and CI.

### Verified procedures and private value reports

Procedure manifests can be verified against exact artifacts and fixtures, then inspected as current, incompatible,
locally modified, unverified, or update-available. Verification is preview-first and never executes downloaded procedures
automatically. Manifest v2 adds bounded discovery metadata plus deterministic stable/preview rollout policy while v1
remains readable for local verification and status.
Exact current manifest, receipt, and strict BOM-free, NUL-free UTF-8 artifact text can be previewed and explicitly published to a
configured Git share; same-version conflicts fail closed and unrelated worktree or staged files remain untouched.
Context Brief admits a bounded task-relevant dependency closure through the public agent catalog, chooses the highest
cohort-admitted semantic version, and exposes distinct Git-share provenance without artifact bodies or executable
commands. Procedure-bearing Context Briefs use response/projector schema v4 and agent-view schema v2; older versions
reject the new field, while unavailable, truncated, or conflicting repository evidence remains an explicit coverage gap.
CLI and MCP publication share the same preview-ID, explicit-approval boundary; pushing remains separately explicit.
The MCP adapters live in the full toolset, preserving the bounded default core schema budget.

`threadnote value report` summarizes the local task-context loop using content-free counts. Its explicit export remains
preview-first and redacted: it excludes queries, memory text, source code, paths, repository names, and stable user IDs.

Recall results now surface `useful`, `wrong`, `pin`, `dismiss`, and distinct `applied` feedback in MCP, CLI guidance,
and Manager; applied means the context materially informed a plan or change. ValueReportV1 remains backward-readable
while adding applied counts/rates, and Manager presents activation, first-evidence timing, second-agent reuse, Knowledge
Delta outcomes, and health resolution. Preview-first retention and category-scoped deletion cover local feedback, value
events, and explicit redacted export bundles without adding any background upload.

### Offline release-readiness evidence

An on-demand eval:threadnote-5-release-readiness harness now validates content-free receipts for the complete local task
loop: solo and two-agent use, Git sharing, offline operation, dirty-worktree abstention, interrupted resume,
upgrade/downgrade compatibility, provider-neutral proposals, and health resolution. Exact candidate versions, commits,
executables, fixtures, source artifacts, and individual observations are hash-bound. Missing, tampered, duplicate, or
mislabeled observations fail closed. Each observation is replayed from a bounded content-free transcript, chained to
the prior transcript, bound to subsystem receipt digests and exact pre/post runtime identity, and covered by an
independently supplied capture-manifest hash; an adapter label is never sufficient evidence.
Proposal/provider-call and verified-procedure execution claims additionally require a separately reviewed content-free
authority manifest; proposal artifacts and constructed verification receipts cannot self-authorize those claims.

Guided activation evidence is replayed from the real receipt transition rules, including the original plan, every
approved transition, the final completed state, and the independently attested second-agent retrieval. Offline and
interrupted/resumed trials must prove those conditions rather than merely label themselves successful, while private
value evidence must remain bound to the exact activation receipt that produced it. This keeps the release gate honest
without retaining task text, repository paths, or memory bodies.

Release-readiness evidence now checks Context Brief budgets, dirty-worktree abstention, guidance projections, and
upgrade/downgrade boundaries through dedicated source adapters. The checks preserve private inputs while producing only
bounded hashes and outcomes. Where a receipt cannot independently prove a claim—such as a cited first plan, rejection of
a stale guidance precondition, or execution by a particular migration runtime—the result remains unknown until external
authority is supplied.

The scorer now makes an honest comparison with the last 4.x release instead of pretending every 5.0 workflow existed
before. The baseline is fixed to Threadnote 4.7.8 and compares only shared evidence: time and estimated tokens to the
first cited correct Context Brief plan, plus raw wrong-memory feedback counts. Setup success, second-agent reuse,
Knowledge Delta completion, and health resolution are reported as not applicable for 4.7.8, so they can never appear as
zero, passed, improved, or regressed. Candidate thresholds still stand on their own and a candidate failure always wins.

Trust requires the exact 4.7.8 version and commit, its platform-specific executable hash, the comparison ledger, and an
independently reviewed ledger hash. Missing, mismatched, or self-declared authority keeps only the genuinely comparable
lanes unknown and cannot admit a release. Each measured candidate contribution still requires at least ten eligible
trials, including at least 9 successful setup attempts out of 10. Fixture replay validates the evaluator but cannot
admit a release; final admission requires independently verified production task-loop receipts. The harness remains
local and offline and adds no release-note or other CI enforcement.

Final local capture now has a content-free retained-receipt verification procedure and an exact 4.7.8
identity-comparison workflow. It extends the task-loop matrix with exact five-field closeout
evidence, verified procedures, activation/ValueReport reuse, provider-neutral proposals, and
read-only local scheduling plus configured Git-team health aggregation. Generic receipt wrappers
and unavailable source-native subsystem records stay explicitly unknown; they can never admit a
release.

Health-maintenance receipts now independently replay the shipped local schedule plan, observed command, and bounded personal/configured-team aggregate. A separately reviewed authority entry, bound to the exact receipt digest, must prove zero writes and network activity plus stable before/after Git HEAD, index, and worktree observations for every selected team; clean, findings, and unknown aggregate results remain distinct.

### Provider-neutral graph machine credentials

Graph and OCI machine helpers now support explicit OAuth 2.0 client-credentials configuration, including Okta custom
authorization servers with path-based issuers, HTTP Basic client authentication, and `cid`/`scp` claims. Generic helper
commands and environment names retain safe Auth0 aliases. Explicit same-origin token/JWKS endpoints and an optional
audience request parameter preserve exact authority, scope, and ten-minute lifetime validation. Publisher preflight and
container wiring use the same provider-neutral contract.
